subject.title: Heartbeat drift fix (PR #39182) causes aggressive retry that blocks Telegram during active conversations

question: Should the remaining fix use the narrow fixed-delay `requests-in-flight` debounce from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89989, a new configurable retry delay, or a broader heartbeat architecture change?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the exact delay/config/default policy affects existing heartbeat responsiveness and channel contention behavior.

options.title: Repair and land the narrow debounce
options.body: Keep the fix focused in the wake layer, require per-target retry timing and live channel proof, and close this issue after merge.

options.title: Add a public retry-delay config
options.body: Expose a new heartbeat config surface only if maintainers accept the added configuration and migration/docs cost.

options.title: Defer to broader heartbeat redesign
options.body: Close or pause the narrow PR and track the symptom under the broader non-blocking or activity-based heartbeat issues.

recommendation.title: Repair and land the narrow debounce
recommendation.body: Keep the fix focused in the wake layer, require per-target retry timing and live channel proof, and close this issue after merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The regression provenance and prior heartbeat scheduler history point to this account as the best available owner for the policy choice.
